Over the past week, rumors about Apple’s upcoming camera-equipped AirPods have been flying thick and fast. Here’s a roundup of everything we’ve learned this week about AirPods Pro with cameras.

Latest news on AirPods Pro with cameras

The news broke on Monday when someone discovered a video in the macOS 26.7 beta showing camera-equipped AirPods. In the clip, a user wearing AirPods Pro holds up a book and asks Siri to remember it via Visual Intelligence.

As seen in the video, the camera-equipped AirPods Pro look almost identical to the current AirPods Pro 3.

Beyond the video, macOS 26.7 also contains a large amount of code related to camera-equipped AirPods, revealing further details about how these AirPods will work.

According to code obtained by 9to5Mac, Apple will use a new framework called AccessorySensorMgrd to control image capture and other functions on the camera-equipped AirPods. In the code, Apple refers to this camera sensor as the "Kino Sensor".

  • Each AirPods Pro earbud has its own independent camera, and the two must be paired to operate and capture simultaneously. AccessorySensorMgrd will stitch the two images into a pair; but if only one image is captured, the framework will automatically generate a blank counterpart image.
  • macOS 26.7 mentions two "capture modes": active and passive. The active mode appears to capture one image from each AirPod, or continuously transmit images at a specified "capture rate".
  • The framework monitors multiple parameters, including image width and height, pixel binning, left/right X/Y offsets, and more.
  • The framework also mentions that AirPods Pro will feature a privacy indicator light that illuminates when the camera is capturing.

Separately, a MacRumors forum member also dug up some resolution information about the AirPods Pro cameras:

Active capture mode captures at a resolution of 640×640, and outputs a processed 1024×1024 image. This means the sampled image data is about 0.4 megapixels, while the output image is slightly over 1 megapixel.

The forum member also revealed further details about "passive mode", which according to the description has a "lower resolution, supporting environmental awareness features". macOS 26 lists five scenarios that trigger passive capture:

  • Ambient sound
  • Audio scene changes
  • Posture changes
  • Head turns
  • "Circular zone, when the user leaves a predefined spatial radius."

Release date for camera-equipped AirPods

With the discovery of this video and the related code in the macOS 26.7 beta, speculation immediately arose that this new product would launch soon, possibly even appearing alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra at next month’s Apple event.

However, according to Bloomberg, that is not the case. In a report published on Wednesday, Mark Gurman noted that the camera-equipped AirPods are still on track for a 2027 release.

Gurman explained that Apple is internally developing two versions of the product:

  • B790: The version shown in the video, essentially an improved AirPods Pro 3 with cameras added.
  • B798: A brand-new generation of AirPods (similar to AirPods Pro 4), also with cameras.

Which version Apple ultimately launches remains unknown, but either way, the earliest we can expect to see it is next year.

The Bloomberg report also reiterated that the AirPods Pro cameras will not be used for taking photos or videos, but are designed to "scan the surrounding environment and provide contextual information for the Siri digital assistant and other AI tools".

Summary

In summary, we’ve gathered a substantial amount of new information about camera-equipped AirPods this week, including product features and operational details.

What do you think about Apple’s idea of adding cameras to AirPods Pro? Do you think it’s a good idea? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
